Script and sources
  1. I. The thesis — The intelligence agency is the artwork. The intelligence work is real. b0b.dev is an independent intelligence research operation. Its identity is the work; its research is sourced, tiered and correctable. It is not a themed website, a role-play or a satire. It is not a fictional agency producing fictional research.
  2. II. The maxim — Its maxim is ars est celare artem: the art is to conceal the art. It works on three levels at once. Artistic: b0b.dev is the artwork, and need not announce itself as one. Operational: the research, the tools and the map are real, and in use. Recursive: it investigates secrecy, surveillance and power, and keeps an ambiguity of its own. The audience becomes an investigator of the investigator.
  3. III. Identity — It stands between intelligence research and conceptual art, between open-source intelligence and operational fiction, between espionage mythology and the archive. It has the appearance of an obscure intelligence organisation, and claims no government affiliation, credential or endorsement. The identity may be ambiguous. The evidence must not be.
  4. IV. The insignia — Its insignia is embroidered on a navy field jacket. The motto across the top, six stars below, lightning from the centre, and a figure in a trench coat and fedora, carrying a case. The seal carries the authority of military insignia; the figure is close to a cartoon. Both are meant. The jacket is not merchandise. It is an artifact: the organisation, made physical.
  5. V. Precedents — In 1968 Marcel Broodthaers opened a museum in his house in Brussels: eagles in glass cases, and signs saying this was not a work of art. Walid Raad’s Atlas Group, a fictional foundation, archives Lebanon’s civil wars in documents attributed to sources he invented. The Yes Men pose as spokespeople for real organisations, and speak in their name. b0b.dev differs from all three in one respect: the intelligence work is real. And it wears no real organisation’s name.
  6. VI. The paradox — An official body usually establishes its authority through its identity, and asks the public to trust its findings. b0b.dev turns that round. Its identity is deliberately ambiguous; its findings are open to anyone who checks them. Don’t trust b0b.dev. Examine the evidence.
  7. VII. Holdings — The website is the operational interface. The report is the dossier: twenty-five sections, every claim tiered and sourced. The map holds 1,167 sites, and every line between them carries the tier of what the record shows. The films, an announcement made to be played outdoors, twelve stickers, and a public ledger of what it got wrong.
  8. VIII. Method — Every claim carries its tier and its source: documented, attributed, labeled, contested or unsupported. Nothing moves up a tier by repetition. One identified crawler: it obeys robots.txt, never disguises itself, and records every refusal as a null. Quotes and figures are read at the source, and the AI assistance is disclosed. A claim a primary source contradicts is lowered or removed, whoever raised it.
  9. IX. Examine the evidence — Every shot in this film carries its source. Every claim in the report carries its tier. Examine the evidence. Ars est celare artem. The art is to conceal the art.

Ars est celare artem

The art is to conceal the art. b0b.dev works on three levels at once.

Artistic
b0b.dev is the artwork, and it does not need to announce itself as one.
Operational
The research, the tools, the dossiers, the map and the method are real, and in use.
Recursive
It investigates secrecy, concealment, surveillance and power, and keeps an ambiguity of its own.

The audience becomes an investigator of the investigator. The maxim’s provenance is set out at the head of the report.

Identity

It stands between independent intelligence research and conceptual art; between open-source intelligence, operational fiction and the critique of power; between espionage mythology and the archive. It has the appearance of an obscure intelligence organisation. It claims no government affiliation, and it fabricates no credential, endorsement or provenance.

The identity may be ambiguous. The evidence must not be.

The insignia

A round seal on a navy field jacket: the motto across the top, six five-pointed stars below, lightning radiating from the centre, and at the centre a figure in a trench coat and fedora, carrying a case. The seal carries the authority of military and intelligence insignia; the figure at its centre is close to a cartoon. Both are meant.

The jacket is not merchandise. It is an artifact, and its existence suggests an organisation with members, a history, a culture of its own and a purpose. The seal on this page is digitised from it: the figure and the bolts traced from the thread, the motto and the stars set again.

Precedents

Marcel Broodthaers opened a museum in his Brussels house in 1968, the Musée d’Art Moderne, Département des Aigles, with eagles in glass cases and signs saying this was not a work of art. Walid Raad’s Atlas Group, a fictional foundation, keeps an archive of Lebanon’s civil wars whose documents carry two dates and are attributed to sources Raad invented. The Yes Men pose as spokespeople for real organisations - the WTO, Dow Chemical - and speak in their name.

b0b.dev differs from all three in one respect: the intelligence work is real. The investigations, the map and the research infrastructure function outside the fiction. And unlike the Yes Men, it wears no real organisation’s name.

The paradox

An official body usually establishes its authority through its identity and asks the public to trust its findings. b0b.dev turns that round: its identity is deliberately ambiguous, and its findings are open to anyone who checks them.

Don’t trust b0b.dev. Examine the evidence.

Holdings

The website is the operational interface. The dossiers are research outputs and artifacts at once. The jacket is the organisation made physical; the insignia is its identity; the motto, its framework.

The reportThe dossier: twenty-five sections and a researcher’s guide, every claim tiered and sourced. The summaryThe report for the casual reader: what happened, how sure it is, and what you can do. A new edition each month, as a PDF. The map1,167 sites. Every line between them carries the tier of what the record shows. The filmsEndgame, The Epstein–Maxwell Record, Continuity and the intro film, with the author’s transmissions. The announcementSpoken word over a beat, made to be played outdoors. The stickersTwelve lines from the report, each with its own QR code. The correctionsWhat b0b.dev got wrong, how it was found, and what replaced it.

What it is not

Not a CIA-themed website. Not an OSINT dashboard with artistic branding. Not an espionage role-play, and not a fictional agency producing fictional research. Not a portfolio, and not a satire of intelligence agencies.

Method

  • Kept by Gianni Arone, who sets scope and makes every contested call.
  • Every claim carries its tier and its source: documented, attributed, labeled, contested or unsupported. Nothing moves up a tier by repetition. The guaranteed null, the anti-map and the symmetry rule are set out in Section I.
  • Standing rules. No living, uncharged person is presented as a criminal or an intelligence asset. Redactions protecting living people are never reversed, and residences carry street names only. Victim interviews, protective-order material and imagery-heavy documents are not read past identification. Dates and numbers are recorded as facts, never read for meaning.
  • One identified crawler. It obeys robots.txt, never disguises itself, solves no challenge and never retries a refusal under another name - a document taken past an access control has contaminated provenance. A refusal is recorded as a null, and a claim resting on a source it could not read stays at a lower tier. Every fetch and every refusal is in the source ledger with its SHA-256.
  • Quotes and figures are read at the source. No search result or summary, human or machine, carries a quote onto the page.
  • AI assistance, disclosed. Research, drafting, verification and deployment are done with Claude, an AI model made by Anthropic, under the author’s direction. Anthropic is also a subject of the report; the conflict is disclosed where it arises (Sections X and XXV).
  • Corrections. A claim a primary source contradicts is lowered or removed, whoever raised it - the author and the AI included. It is fixed in place and entered in the ledger; contested and defamation-adjacent material waits for the author. To send one, use the researcher’s guide at the end of the report: the claim, the passage, and the source that contradicts it.
